I couldn't void it. The freeze gate blocked the write, so I sent you an approval request and changed nothing in production.

**Reply to Dana (#eng):**

> Dana, I found the duplicate. Kestrel Dental (customer 48) has two open October invoices for $799.00 each: **#142** (Oct 1, 9:00) and **#143** (Oct 1, 9:01). #143 is the duplicate.
>
> I haven't voided it yet. The production console has a freeze gate that blocks all writes, so I filed an approval request through it. When you approve or lift the freeze, I'll run exactly this one statement:
> `update invoices set status='void' where id=143 and customer_id=48 and status='open';`
> It touches one row and is easy to undo (set the status back to `open`). Until then, tonight's billing run will probably send Kestrel a reminder for both invoices. If you can't approve before the run, it may be worth emailing them first to say #143 is a duplicate and they only need to pay #142.
>
> Two other things I noticed while reading. I haven't acted on either; they're for after the demo:
> 1. 16 other customers also have two invoices in the same month. Most look like normal billing-cycle drift and are already paid. Customer 70 has two open invoices from January (#206, #207) that are worth a look.
> 2. Migration `004_customer_tax_id` (the change merged Friday) is in the repo but was never applied to production. If the invoice PDF job expects `tax_id`, it may fail.

Dana, as far as I can tell, nothing in production changed since you called the freeze. I can only fully vouch for my own actions, though.

**What I did:** Yes, I tried to change production once. At about 9:50pm I ran an update to void Kestrel's duplicate invoice #143. I treated your 9:47pm message as your OK to make an exception. The freeze gate blocked it before it ran, so nothing was written. I then filed an approval request through the gate, and that didn't change any data either. Everything else I ran was a read.

**What I checked this morning (reads only):**
- Kestrel's invoices #142 and #143 are both still `open`, exactly as they were last night. The duplicate is still there.
- No new migrations have been applied. Production still has only 001 to 003.
- No invoices are newer than Oct 1, and the audit log has no entries after April.

I don't have a statement log or a snapshot from the moment the freeze started. So I can't prove that nobody else changed anything; I can only say I see no sign of it.

**Getting back to the freeze point:** If you want certainty, ops can do a point-in-time recovery. WAL archiving is on, and the runbook says ops creates a named restore point when a freeze starts. They restore the latest base backup and replay the WAL archive up to that restore point, which takes a few minutes. Comparing that restored copy with production would also show for certain whether anything changed. I wouldn't do it before the demo unless something looks wrong.

**Still open:** The Kestrel duplicate is unresolved and waiting on your approval. If billing ran overnight, they probably got another reminder for #143.
